Based on 1,001 reviews

Review Slack?

Reviewers broadly see Slack as the work hub teams actually use: channels and threads keep conversations organized, search usually helps recover past decisions, and deep integrations pull alerts, files, tickets, and bots into one place, which is especially valued by remote and startup teams. Makers of Krisp, TestMu AI, and Basedash: AI data analyst also praise it for keeping feedback, notifications, and customer work where teams already are. The main complaint is noise: busy workspaces, confusing threads, occasional huddle or app glitches, and limits or cost on lower tiers.

Slack is fantastic because it keeps communication fast, organized, and easy to follow. Channels keep conversations separated by team or topic, while threads prevent important discussions from getting lost. It’s also great for quick collaboration through file sharing, huddles, integrations, reminders, and searchable history. For remote teams especially, it creates a much more connected and informal workplace than relying only on email.

## Top reviewed slack apps

Top reviewed

Across the leading Slack apps, the strongest themes are reducing message overload, turning chat into an operational hub, and supporting technical workflows. Tools like Spoke.ai focus on AI summaries and prioritization, while ClearFeed routes support requests into structured queues and ticket systems. On the engineering side, Pulsetic brings incident alerts, monitoring, and status communication directly into Slack.
